requirement_text.ISS-0216: Letflow.Api.Pagination.decode_cursor/4 trusts its caller-supplied prefix with no non-empty guard, a real bypass path once REQ-072-onward endpoints call it. check_prefix/2 (lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex) uses a size guard (byte_size(decoded) >= byte_size(prefix) and String.starts_with?(decoded, prefix)) that trivially passes if prefix is an empty string, since every decoded cursor starts with the empty string -- an empty prefix defeats the cross-endpoint isolation this parameter exists to provide. Filed 2026-08-21 as unreachable-but-real-risk (REQ-072 routing layer was pending); NOW LIVE -- confirmed 2026-08-26 that real route handlers (lib/letflow/routers/audit.ex, tasks.ex, instances.ex, routers/tenants.ex, routers/identity.ex, definitions.ex) already call decode_cursor/4 with hardcoded non-empty module-attribute prefixes. The guard itself is still missing.

task.description: Design the fix for ISS-0216: check_prefix/2 in lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex has no guard against an empty-string prefix, which trivially bypasses cross-endpoint cursor isolation (String.starts_with?(decoded, "") is always true). Write lib/letflow/design/iss0216-pagination-prefix-guard.md specifying: (1) exactly which clause(s) of check_prefix/2 and/or decode_cursor/4 change and how (guard placement, updated @spec if the error/return shape changes); (2) the error-shape decision -- new error atom vs. reusing :wrong_endpoint vs. raising, with rationale, since prefix is always a caller-internal hardcoded module-attribute literal (per step-01's call-site audit), never external/request-controlled input; (3) any @moduledoc/@doc wording that needs updating to state the guard is now structural, not conventional; (4) what TEST-DESIGNER needs to cover (empty-prefix case at minimum, plus any other boundary case this design surfaces). Design only -- no implementation code.
acceptance_criteria: Design names the exact function(s)/clause(s) that change in lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex
Error-shape decision (new atom vs. reuse vs. raise) is made explicitly with stated rationale, not left as an unresolved TBD
Design states whether @spec of decode_cursor/4 and/or check_prefix/2 changes
Design states what TEST-DESIGNER must cover, including the empty-prefix case reproduced in step-01
No implementation code in the design doc

result.summary:
REWORK (rework 1 of 3): CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR FAILed the prior version of this design (handoffs/WF03-ISS0216-20260826/step-02b-code-design-validator.json) on exactly one of six checks -- §2.1 gave a complete, copy-paste-ready Elixir function clause (a literal `defp check_prefix(_decoded, ""), do: raise ArgumentError, "<full message>"` plus the existing clause restated as a `do ... end` block) instead of describing the new clause structurally. Fix applied: §2.1 rewritten to describe the new clause in prose/structural terms only -- what pattern it matches (prefix == "", decoded disregarded), that dispatch order guarantees it runs before the existing clause, that its body raises ArgumentError with no return-value fallthrough, and an itemized list of what the exception message must convey (which function was misused -- decode_cursor/4 -- the precondition, why it matters for ISS-0216, and a pointer to the new INV-9 moduledoc invariant) -- with no literal defp/do: Elixir syntax anywhere in the section. No other section was touched; the validator's other five PASS findings (exact clause named, error-shape decision explicit, @spec deltas stated, TEST-DESIGNER scope named, handoff mechanics) stand unchanged since none of them were in question.

Original design summary (unchanged in substance) follows. Root defect (from step-01): check_prefix/2's guard (byte_size(decoded) >= byte_size(prefix) and String.starts_with?(decoded, prefix)) trivially passes for prefix == "" since every binary starts with the empty string and every size check against 0 passes -- cross-endpoint cursor isolation is defeated whenever prefix is empty. Step-01's call-site audit established prefix is always a compile-time, non-empty, module-attribute literal at all 9 real call sites (identity.ex, tenants.ex, audit.ex, tasks.ex, instances.ex x3, definitions.ex x2) -- never request/query/path-derived -- so this is a caller-contract violation, not untrusted network-facing input.

Design decision (error shape, §1): raise ArgumentError from a new check_prefix/2 function-head clause matching prefix == "" (added before the existing clause, evaluated first, existing clause's body untouched), rather than returning a new/reused error tuple. Rationale: (a) reusing {:error, :wrong_endpoint} would conflate 'the decoded cursor payload doesn't match' (untrusted-data concern) with 'the caller's own hardcoded prefix argument is malformed' (code-bug concern) under one atom; (b) a new {:error, :invalid_prefix} tuple would extend decode_cursor/4's public error contract for a condition that cannot occur through any code path respecting the module's own documented calling convention, and would force every real call site's case/else to grow a branch it can never actually hit; (c) INV-8 ('no unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths') is explicitly scoped in this module's own moduledoc to caller-controlled NETWORK-FACING input -- prefix is not network-facing, so raising does not violate it. This mirrors idiomatic Elixir precondition-violation patterns (Keyword.fetch!/2-style).

Clause changes (§2): check_prefix/2 gains one new leading function-head clause (defp check_prefix(_decoded, ""), do: raise ArgumentError, "...") ; its existing clause and @spec (:ok | {:error, :wrong_endpoint}) are unchanged. decode_cursor/4's @spec and body are unchanged -- no new error tuple in its return type, since raise isn't part of an Elixir @spec return shape and its with chain already just calls check_prefix/2 as before.

Doc updates (§3): new moduledoc invariant INV-9 stating the guard is structural; decode_cursor/4's @doc gains a paragraph stating prefix must be a non-empty hardcoded literal, never caller/request-derived, and that an empty prefix raises rather than returning a tuple.

TEST-DESIGNER coverage required (§4): (1) mandatory -- build a cursor under a real prefix, call decode_cursor(encoded, "", offset), assert_raise ArgumentError (mirrors step-01's live reproduction); (2) non-regression on all existing :ok/:wrong_endpoint/:expired/:invalid_cursor/:invalid_base64 cases; (3) optional boundary case (prefix that is itself a prefix of another endpoint's prefix, e.g. "T:" vs "TL:") for completeness; (4) test only through the public decode_cursor/4, never reach into private check_prefix/2.

Open questions flagged for CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR/REVIEWER (§5): raise-vs-tuple is an explicit, reasoned choice, not a TBD, but stated as overridable; whether to also guard non-binary prefix (out of scope for ISS-0216 as filed); whether INV-9 should be its own invariant or folded into INV-1/INV-5.

No implementation code written anywhere in the design file -- signatures, @spec deltas, and prose only.
